items.title: Hundreds of ships cross the Strait of Hormuz, some are going 'dark' to do it
items.description: Amid new strikes, the future of the Strait of Hormuz has again been plunged into uncertainty, but ships are finding a way through.

items.title: Iran and Israel stop trading blows but fighting continues in Lebanon
items.description: Israel and Iran have agreed to hold off attacks but Iran says it won't "retreat from any threat' with Israel too warning it would "respond with full force" if attacks resumed.

items.title: Property and the budget ease pressure on the RBA
items.description: With two Australian banks cutting fixed home loan rates, there is a ray of hope that the cycle of interest rate hikes has peaked and borrowing costs may be lower down the track — another sign the pace of economic change has moved into overdrive.

items.title: We were happier during the COVID-19 pandemic. The reason is money
items.description: Australians felt a greater sense of satisfaction during the COVID-19 pandemic than they do today, according to government data, as households grapple with the impact of inflation, rising interest rates and a reduction in real wages.

items.title: The AI superpower with no seat at the table
items.description: Taipei sits at the physical centre of the global AI economy but remains shut out of the diplomatic rooms where its sovereign rights are negotiated, often by others.

items.title: Xi and Kim pledge deeper cooperation between China and North Korea
items.description: China and North Korea should strengthen exchanges "in diplomacy, law enforcement, and the military", Chinese leader Xi Jinping has suggested during a rare two-day visit to Pyongyang.

items.title: Young couple told by agent that landlords would not rent to 'people like you'
items.description: Hopeful renters say negative stereotypes about young people are making it almost impossible to secure a rental on the Sunshine Coast.

items.title: The most contentious parts of the NDIS bill being scrutinised today
items.description: Politicians are presiding over three days of public hearings into a bill paving the way for the biggest ever cuts to the NDIS.

items.title: Four-time veterans to late bolters, here's your Socceroos pocket guide
items.description: Mat Ryan and Mathew Leckie are at a record-equalling fourth FIFA World Cup, while Cristian Volpato headlines a host of first-timers, after his late switch from Italy. Here's your complete guide to the Socceroos' World Cup squad.

items.title: Richard Scolyer remembered by peers for contributions to cancer treatment
items.description: Before being diagnosed with cancer, the 2024 Australian of the Year was a leading melanoma researcher, developing better therapies for those with the disease.

items.title: Melbourne's data centre boom sparks fire fears
items.description: Serious concerns about an influx of large-scale data centres in Melbourne's west are being raised by Fire Rescue Victoria insiders.

items.title: As One Nation nips at his heels the PM has no choice but to play the long game
items.description: The government is playing a long game in responding to the surge of support for One Nation. It has little other choice.

items.title: 'Everything's on hold': Patients caught in surgery backlog
items.description: Patients are waiting years for elective surgery as delays and cancellations mount in Tasmania — can the health system handle the $700 million of cuts still to come?

items.title: SA farmers celebrate dramatic turnaround after record rain
items.description: Twelve months after drought left paddocks bare, record rainfall in parts of South Australia has left some farmers smiling at significant improvements.

items.title: Heated Rivalry meets Yellowface in Josh Silver's debut novel, Fruit Fly
items.description: Described as one of the books of the year, Fruit Fly asks who has the right to tell which stories in an age of cancellation for cultural appropriation.

items.title: Your rights and options if you find mould in your rental
items.description: Who is responsible for a mould issue depends on a few factors, but experts say it is worth acting early on.

items.title: Kings and Queens quiz: Where is Prince Harry in the royal line of succession?
items.description: The latest ABC More or Less quiz challenges you to rank some of the most famous (and infamous) royals in history, and sort some of the current crop.

items.title: At least 35 dead after magnitude-7.8 earthquake hits Philippines
items.description: At least 35 people have been killed in a magnitude-7.8 earthquake that shook the Mindanao region in the southern Philippines, with a tsunami possible on some regional coasts.

items.title: Pope Leo meets abuse victims in Spain while some protest
items.description: The pontiff, who is on a week-long visit to Spain, has listened to proposals to make safeguarding more effective.

items.title: A 'ring of fire' could soon burn around one of Australia's major cities
items.description: Australian states are pushing ahead with waste-to-energy incineration despite significant opposition. It means one capital city will soon be surrounded by a "ring of fire".

items.title: Undersea volcano inundates island with 'desert' of stone
items.description: Residents are concerned about access to food and fresh water as pumice stone makes travel difficult for Papua New Guinea's seafaring communities.

items.title: Mihocek experienced 'lack of feeling' before hospital visit says coach
items.description: Melbourne claims an eight-point win over Collingwood at the MCG as Brody Mihocek is taken to hospital after a serious injury.

items.title: Blues centre Stephen Crichton ruled out of State of Origin II
items.description: New South Wales have been dealt an injury blow ahead of State of Origin with Stephen Crichton ruled out of the squad due to a shoulder injury.

items.title: Script reveals methods of Cambodian centre scamming Australians
items.description: Australian and Thai police release a script discovered in a Cambodian scam compound, revealing the high-pressure methods used to coerce Australian victims.

items.title: Sentencing of officer Benedict Bryant a rare moment of accountability
items.description: Inside a quiet district courtroom in the heart of Sydney’s bustling CBD, a historic moment has unfolded involving a NSW Police sergeant.
